This factsheet clarifies several points about the upcoming UK-EU Summit 2026 package, set to be announced on November 20th.

While leaving the EU is not the sole cause of small boat crossings, the UK Government’s view is that leaving made tackling the issue harder by reducing access to intelligence and returns mechanisms.

Leaving the European Union reduced the UK’s access to shared EU security information on those crossing the Channel, removed existing mechanisms to return migrants, and meant the UK has had to focus on negotiating new bilateral agreements—including with France, Belgium, and Germany.

No one is saying leaving the EU is the sole reason behind small boat crossings, and the Prime Minister has been clear that this is not an excuse to avoid taking the necessary action to secure and restore control to the UK’s borders.
